mit-non-nau-canh-ca-chuon-quang-nam.name: Quảng Nam young jackfruit and flying-fish soup
aliases: Young jackfruit soup with flying fish
Quảng Nam jackfruit and fish soup
mit-non-nau-canh-ca-chuon-quang-nam.serving_basis: One pot for four people, shared with hot rice as part of a family meal.
mit-non-nau-canh-ca-chuon-quang-nam.description: This rustic soup pairs young jackfruit from the garden with flying fish from Quảng Nam’s coast. The fruit turns tender and nearly translucent while the fish gives the broth gentle sweetness. Bếp Việt adapts the water and seasoning for a home-sized pot, keeping the broth light.
mit-non-nau-canh-ca-chuon-quang-nam.finished_dish: Pale golden young-jackfruit wedges and intact cooked flying-fish pieces sit in lightly golden broth, finished with scallion and herbs.
mit-non-nau-canh-ca-chuon-quang-nam.serving: Ladle broth and solids into bowls and serve hot with steamed rice. Offer green-chili fish sauce separately if desired; season lightly so the jackfruit remains distinct.
tips: If handling fresh jackfruit, lightly oil the knife and hands to reduce sticky sap; soak the cut pieces in lightly salted water and rinse.
Choose fresh flying fish or fish cleaned by the seller; remove gills and entrails and pat dry.
Add fish first and stir gently; add jackfruit once the fish begins to firm so the pieces do not break.
mit-non-nau-canh-ca-chuon-quang-nam.image_alt: A bowl of Quảng Nam young jackfruit soup with cooked flying fish, scallion and fresh herbs.
mit-non-nau-canh-ca-chuon-quang-nam.time_note: About 45 minutes to prepare the ingredients and simmer the soup.

ingredients.name: Cleaned flying fish
ingredients.notes: Select fresh fish, remove gills and entrails; cut into serving pieces.

ingredients.name: Peeled young jackfruit
ingredients.notes: Weigh the edible portion.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add enough to mostly cover the ingredients.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush or slice.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For lightly frying the shallot.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Start modestly and adjust.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: For seasoning the fish and soup.

ingredients.name: Green chili
ingredients.notes: Optional; leave whole or lightly crush.

ingredients.name: Scallion
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese coriander
ingredients.notes: Wash, chop and add at the end.

preparation_steps: Lightly oil the knife if preparing fresh jackfruit. Remove skin and fibrous core, cut into 2 cm pieces, soak in lightly salted water for 10 minutes, rinse and drain.
Rinse the fish, remove gills and entrails if needed, pat dry and cut into pieces. Season with some salt and fish sauce for 10 minutes.
Peel and crush the shallot; wash and slice the herbs. Bring a pot of water to a gentle boil.
cooking_steps: Warm the oil and briefly fry the shallot. Add fish and gently turn for 2–3 minutes until the surface firms.
Add hot water, bring to a gentle boil, lower the heat and simmer the fish for 7–8 minutes; skim foam if needed.
Add young jackfruit and simmer for 12–15 minutes until tender but not falling apart. Season with remaining fish sauce and salt.
Turn off the heat, add scallion and Vietnamese coriander, and ladle without stirring hard.

thit-kho-mam-ruoc-hue.name: Hue braised pork belly with fermented shrimp paste
aliases: Hue pork belly braised with mắm ruốc
thit-kho-mam-ruoc-hue.serving_basis: A savory braise for four, served with rice and vegetables.
thit-kho-mam-ruoc-hue.description: Pork belly is first browned so some fat renders, then gently braised with lemongrass, garlic and thinned mắm ruốc. Bếp Việt moderates the salt and sweetness so the paste’s distinctive aroma stays clear without becoming harsh.
thit-kho-mam-ruoc-hue.finished_dish: Amber-brown pork cubes are coated in glossy reduced shrimp-paste sauce, fragrant with lemongrass and garlic and lightly accented with chili.
thit-kho-mam-ruoc-hue.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, cucumber or boiled greens. The braise is already savory; use a clean spoon for leftovers.
tips: Mắm ruốc varies in saltiness; dilute and strain if needed, then season with only part of the amount first.
Render pork over medium heat; drain some fat if necessary but keep a little to fry the aromatics.
Braise over low heat until the sauce coats the pork; do not cook it completely dry.
search_terms: pork belly braised with shrimp paste
thit-kho-mam-ruoc-hue.image_alt: A rustic clay pot of Hue pork belly braised with mắm ruốc, lemongrass, garlic and chili.
thit-kho-mam-ruoc-hue.time_note: About 65 minutes including a brief 10-minute seasoning rest.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Choose an even balance of lean meat and fat; cut into 2 cm cubes.

ingredients.name: Hue mắm ruốc
ingredients.notes: Dissolve in warm water, let settle and strain; saltiness varies.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Mince half and slice the rest.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Fresh coconut water
ingredients.notes: Optional; hot water may be used instead.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Start small and adjust at the end.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add only after tasting the shrimp paste.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Use less if the pork renders a lot of fat.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Optional.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Finish with a light sprinkle.

preparation_steps: Rinse and dry the pork, then cut into bite-sized cubes. Mince lemongrass, garlic and shallot; reserve some sliced lemongrass.
Dissolve shrimp paste in 40 ml warm water and let settle, then strain or pour off the smooth portion. Measure coconut water and sugar.
cooking_steps: Brown pork in a heavy pot over medium heat for 8–10 minutes until the edges color and fat renders. Drain excess fat if needed, leaving about a tablespoon.
Fry minced lemongrass, garlic and shallot in the remaining fat until fragrant. Return the pork and stir.
Add strained shrimp paste, sugar and coconut water. Simmer gently over low heat for 18–22 minutes until tender and coated in sauce.
Taste before adding fish sauce. Add chili, pepper and sliced lemongrass; turn off the heat while the sauce is still moist.

trung-vit-lon-um-bau-hue.name: Hue duck eggs um with bottle gourd
aliases: Hue duck eggs braised with bottle gourd
trung-vit-lon-um-bau-hue.serving_basis: A small pot for four, served hot as a savory soup or light evening dish with rice.
trung-vit-lon-um-bau-hue.description: Duck eggs are um-cooked with young bottle gourd, Hue fermented shrimp paste, ginger and Vietnamese coriander. Bếp Việt adapts a small home batch and seasons it gently so the gourd’s sweetness balances the rich eggs and mild salty heat.
trung-vit-lon-um-bau-hue.finished_dish: A hot bowl of fully cooked duck eggs and tender pale-green bottle-gourd pieces in broth scented with ginger and Vietnamese coriander.
trung-vit-lon-um-bau-hue.serving: Ladle eggs, gourd and broth into bowls. Offer lemon-pepper salt separately if desired; serve immediately while hot.
tips: Choose eggs from a traceable source, wash the shells and boil thoroughly before peeling; remove shell fragments.
Dilute the shrimp paste and add it gradually because salt levels vary.
Add Vietnamese coriander, scallion and ginger near the end; cook the gourd until just tender.
search_terms: Hue duck eggs and bottle gourd
duck eggs braised with bottle gourd
trung-vit-lon-um-bau-hue.image_alt: A bowl of Hue duck eggs um with bottle gourd, ginger, Vietnamese coriander and warm broth.
trung-vit-lon-um-bau-hue.time_note: About 40 minutes to boil the eggs, prepare the gourd and finish the um.

ingredients.name: Balut duck eggs
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh eggs and refrigerate as directed by the seller.

ingredients.name: Young bottle gourd
ingredients.notes: Peel, remove mature seeds if present and cut into 1 cm pieces.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add more hot water if a soupier result is preferred.

ingredients.name: Hue mắm ruốc
ingredients.notes: Dilute and add gradually to taste.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Mince half and cut the rest into thin strips.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Scallion
ingredients.notes: Wash and slice.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese coriander
ingredients.notes: Wash and roughly chop.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying aromatics.

ingredients.name: Chili powder
ingredients.notes: Optional.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Begin with a small amount.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Finish to taste.

preparation_steps: Wash eggshells and place eggs in a pot covered with cold water. Bring to a boil, reduce to medium and cook for 18–20 minutes; cool slightly, peel carefully and remove shell fragments.
Peel and cut the gourd. Mince shallot and part of the ginger; cut the rest into strips. Dilute shrimp paste with two tablespoons of warm water.
cooking_steps: Fry shallot, minced ginger and chili powder for 30–45 seconds without browning. Add gourd, turn gently for one minute and season with a little salt and shrimp paste.
Pour in hot water, bring to a gentle boil and simmer 5–7 minutes until the gourd is nearly tender.
Add peeled eggs, lower the heat and um for 4–5 minutes so they heat through. Do not stir vigorously.
Taste, add pepper, ginger strips, scallion and Vietnamese coriander; serve hot.

canh-la-lang-xu-quynh.name: Quỳnh Lưu la lằng soup with shrimp
canh-la-lang-xu-quynh.serving_basis: One pot for four, served hot with steamed rice.
canh-la-lang-xu-quynh.description: La lằng leaves have a gentle bitterness and are used in Quỳnh Lưu, Nghệ An, for a simple soup, especially in hot weather. Bếp Việt adapts a home pot with fresh shrimp and tomatoes. Use only leaves identified and sold as food by a trusted supplier; do not gather unidentified wild leaves.
canh-la-lang-xu-quynh.finished_dish: Dark-green chopped la lằng leaves with cooked pink shrimp and softened tomato in a clear broth, pleasantly bitter with a light savory finish.
canh-la-lang-xu-quynh.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice; it pairs well with fried fish and pickled vegetables. Cook only enough for the meal.
tips: Use only la lằng leaves correctly identified and sold for food by a trusted source; do not substitute unidentified wild leaves.
Add the leaves near the end and avoid prolonged boiling.
If using dried shrimp, soak them first and reduce salt or fish sauce.
canh-la-lang-xu-quynh.image_alt: A bowl of Quỳnh Lưu la lằng soup with fresh shrimp and tomato in a light broth.
canh-la-lang-xu-quynh.time_note: About 27 minutes to prepare the leaves and shrimp and simmer the soup.

ingredients.name: Food-grade la lằng leaves
ingredients.notes: Use leaves correctly identified and sold for food; wash thoroughly.

ingredients.name: Peeled fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Devein, rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: Small tomatoes
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into wedges.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the preferred broth level.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying shallot and tomatoes.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season lightly and adjust at the end.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season modestly.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Optional.

preparation_steps: Remove wilted leaves, rinse several times under clean running water, drain and slice. Peel and devein shrimp, rinse and drain; cut tomatoes into wedges.
Mince shallot. Keep tools separate for raw shrimp or wash immediately after preparation.
cooking_steps: Heat oil and fry shallot until fragrant. Add tomatoes and cook for 2–3 minutes until softened.
Add water and bring to a boil. Add shrimp and cook 3–4 minutes until opaque and fully cooked.
Add la lằng leaves and return to a boil for 1–2 minutes. Season with fish sauce, salt and pepper, tasting for gentle bitterness without excess salt.
Turn off the heat, ladle into a bowl and serve hot.

thit-luoc-tom-chua-hue.name: Hue boiled pork with fermented sour shrimp
aliases: Hue-style boiled pork with fermented shrimp
Pork and fig wraps with sour shrimp paste
Boiled pork served with Hue sour shrimp paste
thit-luoc-tom-chua-hue.serving_basis: A shared platter for four, served with vegetables and rice paper for wrapping.
thit-luoc-tom-chua-hue.description: Tender boiled pork belly is served with Hue fermented sour shrimp, fig, green banana, pineapple and herbs for rice-paper wraps. Bếp Việt adapts the portions for a family table, balancing rich pork, tangy shrimp, astringent fig and fresh vegetables.
thit-luoc-tom-chua-hue.finished_dish: Thin slices of boiled pork are arranged beside pink-red fermented shrimp, fig and green-banana slices, pineapple, cucumber, fresh herbs and rice paper.
thit-luoc-tom-chua-hue.serving: Wrap pork with herbs, fig and pineapple and dip lightly in the sour shrimp. The condiment is already strongly seasoned, so no extra salty sauce is needed.
tips: Use ready-to-eat fermented shrimp with clear labeling, source and expiry date; refrigerate as directed and serve with a clean spoon.
Add pork to boiling water, then simmer gently until the center is fully cooked; time depends on thickness.
Rest the pork for 5–10 minutes before slicing so the pieces stay neat and juicy.
search_terms: Hue boiled pork with tôm chua
thit-luoc-tom-chua-hue.image_alt: A Hue platter of sliced boiled pork with fermented sour shrimp, fig, green banana, pineapple, greens and rice paper.
thit-luoc-tom-chua-hue.time_note: About 50 minutes to prepare accompaniments, boil and rest the pork, and arrange the platter.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Choose a balanced piece with lean meat and fat; rinse well.

ingredients.name: Ready-to-eat Hue fermented shrimp
ingredients.notes: Use a traceable product within its date and store as directed.

ingredients.name: Fresh figs
ingredients.notes: Rinse and slice; briefly soak in lightly salted lemon water.

ingredients.name: Green banana
ingredients.notes: Peel and slice; soak in lightly salted lemon water and drain.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.notes: Peel, remove eyes and slice for wrapping.

ingredients.name: Cucumber
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into sticks.

ingredients.name: Lettuce and fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: Wash thoroughly and drain well.

ingredients.name: Thin rice paper
ingredients.notes: Choose a food-safe brand suitable for wrapping.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Crush and add to the boiling water.

ingredients.name: Dried shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the pork-boiling water.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Enough to cover the pork.

preparation_steps: Rinse the pork. If the piece is very thin, roll and tie loosely with food-safe kitchen twine for easier slicing. Rinse and crush ginger and shallot.
Wash herbs, cucumber, pineapple and figs. Cut cucumber into sticks, pineapple into slices, and fig and green banana into thin slices; soak separately in lightly salted lemon water, then drain.
cooking_steps: Bring water to a boil with ginger, shallot and salt. Add pork; once it returns to a boil, lower the heat, skim foam and simmer 20–25 minutes depending on thickness until fully cooked.
Turn off the heat and leave pork in the hot water for five minutes. Remove, rest 5–10 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain.
Arrange pork, herbs, fig, banana, pineapple, cucumber, rice paper and fermented shrimp separately on a platter.
Wrap pork with vegetables, fig and pineapple in rice paper, dip lightly in fermented shrimp and eat immediately.
